vulnerability.title: Guzzle's cURL handlers leave a first-class Proxy-Authorization header in CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER before 7.14.2, disclosing the proxy credential to origin servers
vulnerability.category_l2: proxy credential placed in the origin header list and sent to the origin server

severity.source: VulnCheck (CNA) publishes CVSS 4.0 6.9 MEDIUM; NVD carries the same VulnCheck CVSS 3.1 5.3 MEDIUM and CVSS 4.0 6.9 MEDIUM as Secondary metrics; OSV GHSA database_specific severity MODERATE — every source rates it medium/moderate

fix_commits.message: Never send first-class `Proxy-Authorization` headers to origins (#3876)

fixed_releases.verified_content: Tag 7.14.2 peels to fa88c578. src/Handler/CurlFactory.php blob 4ee3377 is byte-identical to the post-fix blob in commit 9e4580d4 (its diff header reads index b7bc930..4ee3377). In 7.14.2 applyHeaders() skips a Proxy-Authorization header before serialising (lines 1980-1986), applyManagedProxyAuthorization() routes managed values to CURLOPT_PROXYHEADER with CURLHEADER_SEPARATE, and StreamHandler.php removes the field before route selection.

vulnerability.vulnerable_commit_basis: tag 7.4.4 peels to e3ff079b, inside the advisory range <7.14.2; its src/Handler/CurlFactory.php blob 0c45089f serialises every request header, Proxy-Authorization included, into CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER and contains no CURLOPT_PROXYHEADER/CURLHEADER_SEPARATE handling anywhere in src/

location.verification_method: Static read of src/Handler/CurlFactory.php and src/Handler/StreamHandler.php at tag 7.4.4 and 7.14.2, the fix commit's diff against its parent, the 7.14.2 test file, and the saved advisory records. No PHP code was run and no request was made.

critical_operation.description: applyHeaders copies every header of the PSR-7 request into libcurl's origin header list (CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER) with no awareness of Proxy-Authorization. At 7.4.4 the file contains no CURLOPT_PROXYHEADER, CURLOPT_HEADEROPT or CURLHEADER_SEPARATE reference at all, so a first-class Proxy-Authorization value can only reach libcurl through CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER; libcurl's default CURLHEADER_UNIFIED then sends it to the origin server as well as to any proxy. The credential is therefore disclosed to a party it was never meant for, including an attacker-controlled origin that can log request headers.

entry_point.description: '_headers' => $easy->request->getHeaders() — the request's first-class headers, including any Proxy-Authorization set on the PSR-7 request, through client defaults, the headers option or middleware, are what applyHeaders later serialises. The advisory states this is a documented configuration, not misuse.

trace.description: all request headers are captured into the configuration array
each header, including Proxy-Authorization, is appended to $conf[CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER] with no special case
CURLOPT_PROXY may be set from the proxy option, but no proxy header channel is configured, so the header list remains origin-bound under libcurl's default CURLHEADER_UNIFIED
the stream handler only appends a Proxy-Authorization line derived from proxy URL userinfo; it never removes a first-class Proxy-Authorization from the origin-bound header list

source_crosscheck.notes: Every published level is medium/moderate: GHSA MODERATE (CVSS 3.1 5.3), CNA VulnCheck CVSS 4.0 6.9 MEDIUM, NVD Secondary 5.3 and 6.9 MEDIUM. CWE-200 is published by the CNA, NVD and OSV; OSV additionally lists CWE-201 and CWE-522, which are refinements rather than contradictions. The affected range is <7.14.2 in both the CNA record and OSV, and 7.4.4 is inside it. The fix is content-verified by blob identity between commit 9e4580d4 and tag 7.14.2. The CNA is VulnCheck, not the Guzzle vendor, and NVD has not yet analysed the record (no CPE), so the fix/range confidence comes from the git objects rather than from NVD mapping.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read src/Handler/CurlFactory.php at tag 7.4.4 and confirm that applyHeaders serialises every request header into CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER and that nothing in src/ routes Proxy-Authorization to CURLOPT_PROXYHEADER.
An independent reviewer must confirm 7.14.2 is the first fixed release and that its CurlFactory.php blob matches the fix commit 9e4580d4.

An independent reviewer must assess whether the flawed behaviour at 7.4.4 matches the advisory's description (the advisory is written against later 7.x code where a prediction-based migration exists) and whether the disclosure to the origin is real at this version.
An independent reviewer must decide whether the VulnCheck CNA/advisory counts as independent analysis; if not, evidence_independent is false and the entry stays below grade A.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No PHP code was executed and no request was made: the origin-bound header list is read from the cURL option assembly, not reproduced against a live proxy.
Applications that never set a first-class Proxy-Authorization header are unaffected; the advisory states this explicitly, so the flaw requires that documented configuration.

The advisory's narrative describes a later code shape (a migration that runs only when Guzzle predicts a proxy). At 7.4.4 that migration does not exist at all, so the vulnerable state is simpler but the exact mechanism differs from the advisory wording; the reviewer must judge whether it is the same root cause.
NVD status is Awaiting Analysis with no CPE configurations, so the affected-product mapping rests on the CNA record, OSV and the git tags.
The fix commit also hardens the stream handler and adds extensive tests; only the cURL handler path is analysed in depth here.
Whether a real origin actually logs or exposes request headers depends on the deployment; the entry claims disclosure, not exploitation of the credential.
open_questions: Whether libcurl's default CURLHEADER_UNIFIED really forwards CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER lines to an HTTP proxy as well as the origin in every supported libcurl version, which affects the precise disclosure path.
Whether Guzzle 7.4.4 ever sets CURLOPT_PROXYHEADER through CurlVersion options in a way the grep for CURLOPT_PROXYHEADER would have missed (no match was found in src/).
Whether other 7.x branches (for example 7.9.x) received an earlier partial fix that would make the first-affected version later than 0.
